idea: firms issue shares when they are overvalued and buy them back when undervalued; investors under-react to these managerial signals, so net issuers underperform and repurchasers outperform for years (one-year window, Pontiff-Woodgate horizon).
rationale_data: cap and returns (price-volume data, every region): market value growth not explained by returns is net issuance minus payouts
rationale_operators: log(cap / ts_delay(cap, k)) - ts_sum(log(1 + returns), k) is the composite issuance of Daniel-Titman; the minus sign shorts issuers and buys repurchasers; group_rank by country compares firms within their own market and currency

idea: stocks tend to outperform in the same calendar month in which they outperformed in earlier years (earnings announcement timing, fiscal-year flows and recurring demand): the next month's return in each of the last five years predicts this year's.
rationale_operators: ts_sum(ts_delay(returns, 231 + 252k), 21) is the return over the coming month k+1 years ago; add(..., filter=true) averages the five years and keeps stocks with shorter histories; group_rank by country

expression: group_rank(ts_mean(if_else(open > ts_delay(close, 1), if_else(close < open, 1, 0), 0), 21) / ts_mean(ts_mean(if_else(open > ts_delay(close, 1), if_else(close < open, 1, 0), 0), 21), 252), country)
idea: a month with many days of overnight gains followed by daytime losses is a tug of war between overnight noise traders and daytime arbitrageurs; the arbitrageurs over-correct a persistent overnight price pressure, so the most intense tug of war predicts higher returns.
rationale_data: open and close (price-volume data, every region): the overnight return is open over the previous close, the daytime return close over open
rationale_operators: if_else marks days with a positive overnight and a negative daytime return; ts_mean over 21 days is the month's frequency, divided by its own 12-month average as in the paper; rank orders stocks; group_rank by country

idea: a week of unusually high trading volume makes a stock more visible to investors (Merton's investor recognition), which raises demand and returns over the following month; the premium exists in 41 countries.
rationale_operators: ts_mean(volume, 5) over the 50 days before it measures abnormal weekly volume; group_rank by country; decay 6 holds the position for about a month
